specification.problem: Factor N=p1*p2 using quantum order finding for a coprime a, with classical post-processing that also exploits odd orders: when a is a perfect square a=b^2, odd r still gives factors via b^r, and failed runs are reused through order relations involving sqrt(a).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: N=21 with a=4 (square, b=2, order r=3, odd, so the odd-order extension applies), plus a standard non-square control case such as N=15, a=7 (r=4). The scope covers the textbook phase-estimation circuit (t control qubits, n work qubits), continued-fraction order extraction, the odd-order gcd rule for square a, and the check of x^2=1 relations. The two-run relation-combining techniques and the efficiency/probability analysis are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: Multiplicative order of a mod N
Classical integer square root of a when a=b^2 (as integers)

symbols.domain: positive integer, about 2n or fewer if the qubit cap requires

symbols.meaning: Measured control register integer, little-endian: y=sum_i c_i 2^i for measured bit c_i of control qubit i
Random integer in the eigenphase s/r
Modular multiplication |x> -> |a x mod N> on the work register; the black box is its controlled powers
symbols.domain: unitary on n qubits, acts as identity on x>=N

equations.label: Order definition
equations.description: The order that the QOFA computes.
equations.abstract_quote: the smallest integer, $r$, satisfying $a^{r}\mod N=1$, where $a$ is a randomly chosen integer coprime to $N$

equations.label: Even-order factor extraction
equations.description: For even r the factors are obtained from gcds. The method succeeds only if a^{r/2} is not congruent to -1 mod N.
equations.abstract_quote: the factors are given by $p_{1}=\gcd(a^{\frac{r}{2}}-1,N)$ and $p_{2}=\gcd(a^{\frac{r}{2}}+1,N)$
equations.justification: Given in the abstract; the nontriviality condition is standard background.

equations.label: Phase estimation outcome distribution
equations.description: Distribution of the control-register outcome after controlled U_a^{2^j}, inverse QFT, and measurement, starting from work register |1>. Candidate r is the denominator of the continued-fraction convergent of y/2^t with denominator < N, verified by a^r mod N = 1.
equations.justification: Textbook Shor order finding; the abstract does not give the circuit.
assumptions: Controlled U_a^{2^j} from control qubit j
Qiskit little-endian: y bit i is the result of measure(i,i)

equations.label: Odd order with square coprime
equations.latex: a=b^{2},\ r\text{ odd}\Rightarrow (b^{r})^{2}\equiv a^{r}\equiv 1 \pmod N,\quad f_{\pm}=\gcd(b^{r}\mp 1,N)
equations.description: If a is a perfect square and r is odd, then b^r is a square root of 1 mod N (an integer, unlike a^{r/2}); it yields factors when b^r != +-1 mod N.
equations.abstract_quote: the factors can sometimes be found from odd orders if the coprime is square
equations.justification: The abstract notes this possibility; the explicit formula is derived from b^2=a and a^r=1.
assumptions: b computed classically as an exact integer square root of a
b^r not congruent to +-1 mod N

equations.label: Order of the square root
equations.description: Since b^2=a, the order of b divides 2r and is either r or 2r. A found order r for a gives a relation for b, and this is the kind of new order-finding relation a failed run may supply. If r_b=2r is even, gcd(b^{r}\pm 1,N) applies.
equations.abstract_quote: looking out for new order finding relations in the case of failure
equations.justification: This is my reading of the second technique as relating orders of a and sqrt(a); the exact procedure in the paper is not known.

equations.label: Nontrivial square root of unity gives factors
equations.description: Any nontrivial square root of 1 mod N gives a factor of N. This is the final classical check for all cases.
equations.justification: Standard number theory for N=p1 p2 with distinct odd primes.
assumptions: N is a product of two distinct odd primes

registers.name: control
registers.role: Phase-estimation register; H on all qubits, controlled U_a^{2^j}, inverse QFT, then measured

registers.name: work
registers.size: n=ceil(log2 N) (5 for N=21, 4 for N=15)
registers.role: Holds |1> initially; the opaque controlled-U_a^{2^j} black boxes act here; not measured

specification.initial_state: control in |0...0>, work in |1> (little-endian, work qubit 0 set to 1); H applied to every control qubit.

steps.description: Pick the instance (N,a); for a square a, compute b=sqrt(a) classically. Prepare work=|1> and apply H to all t control qubits.
For j=0..t-1 apply controlled-U_a^{2^j} (one black-box query each, control qubit j, target work register).
Apply the inverse QFT to the control register (H, controlled-phase, swaps), with attention to little-endian ordering, then measure only the control qubits.
Classical: convert counts to y, run continued fractions on y/2^t, test candidates r (and small multiples) with a^r mod N=1.
If r is even and a^{r/2} != -1, use the gcd formulas. If r is odd and a=b^2, use the b^r gcds. If r_b=2r, test b^r. Otherwise record the relation and retry with a different a.

specification.measurement: Measure the t control qubits only, with measure(i,i); in a Qiskit counts key the last character is bit 0.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Continued fractions on y/2^t, verification of a^r mod N=1 (also try multiples and divisors of r), then gcd steps from eq_2, eq_4, and eq_6. For non-square a with odd r the abstract does not clearly show a way to find factors; the sketch's suggestion is unverified.
assumptions: Instance N=21, a=4 chosen by me as the smallest useful odd-order square example, plus N=15, a=7 as a control case.
The black box is controlled multiplication by a^{2^j} mod N and is used as given.
The qubit cap allows t+n qubits; for N=21 t may need to be reduced, so the outcome would be coarser.
The sketch's claim about x=a^{(r+1)/2} for non-square a is not adopted as an equation; it is unestablished.
missing_information: The abstract does not give the exact procedure for combining relations across runs.
The abstract does not give the success-probability formulas or the efficiency comparison.
The circuit details (t, QFT variant) are not specified.
